changes.question: training_opt_out
changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-09-11 (quote not found on page; was partial): "If you submit an objection after a training run has started, we may still use your information for that training run, but we will not use it for future training." at https://mbasic.facebook.com/privacy/genai/?locale=en_US | Opt-out is an 'objection request' form submitted while logged in to a Facebook, Instagram or Meta account (a separate form for WhatsApp), not an in-product toggle; it applies to the account and its Accounts Centre accounts, only to future training, and the GenAI page says the appropriate forms depend on your region.

changes.question: business_no_training
changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-09-11 (quote not found on page; was no): "Information from third parties that provide content, including information from products and services built by external developers using our free models provided through APIs" at https://mbasic.facebook.com/privacy/genai/?locale=en_US | The GenAI privacy page lists information from products and services built by external developers on Meta's free API models as a training source and states no exclusion, which the revised rubric scores as NO. The sentence frames these as 'third parties that provide content', so it may describe developers who choose to contribute data, and Meta's separate Llama API and Business AI terms are JavaScript-rendered and could not be checked, hence medium confidence. No fetchable document offers a training exclusion for business or enterprise customers.

changes.question: data_export
changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-09-11 (quote not found on page; was yes): "You have rights to view and download the information that we have about you" at https://mbasic.facebook.com/privacy/policy/printable/?locale=en_US | Self-service 'Download your information' and 'Port your information' tools are listed in the Privacy Policy for all users; the fetchable documents do not explicitly confirm that Meta AI conversations are included in the download.

changes.question: rights_channel
changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-09-11 (quote not found on page; was yes): "To exercise your rights, visit our Help Centres, your settings for Facebook and Instagram and your device-based settings." at https://mbasic.facebook.com/privacy/policy/printable/?locale=en_US | In-product tools (Access, Download, Port, Delete your information) are documented for all users, plus an online contact form and postal address (Meta Platforms, Inc., Privacy Operations, Menlo Park); the AI-training objection form is separate and region-dependent.

changes.question: no_training_default
changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-09-11 (quote not found on page; was no): "To do that, we use your Alexa requests to train our speech recognition and natural language understanding systems using machine learning." at https://www.amazon.co.uk/b?ie=UTF8&node=27246937031 | Amazon's Alexa Privacy Hub states Alexa requests are used to train Alexa systems, and the settings guide says all voice recordings are saved by default with a separate opt-out toggle ('Use voice recordings' / 'Use messages to improve transcriptions' under Help Improve Alexa). Source is the UK regional hub describing classic Alexa data flows; Alexa+-specific LLM training is not addressed in any fetchable Amazon document.

changes.question: training_opt_out
changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-09-11 (quote not found on page; was partial): "If you would rather not have your requests used for this purpose, it’s easy to opt out:" at https://www.amazon.co.uk/b?ie=UTF8&node=27246936031 | A self-service opt-out is documented (Alexa Privacy Settings or app > More > Alexa Privacy > Manage Your Alexa Data > Help Improve Alexa: switch off 'Use voice recordings' and 'Use messages to improve transcriptions', or say 'Alexa, turn off human review of my voice recordings'), and the UK hub says it stops requests being used 'for this purpose', meaning training and human review. Its documented scope is voice recordings and Alexa messages; the pages predate Alexa+ and do not say whether typed Alexa+ chats in the app or on Alexa.com, or shared documents and photos, are covered, so the exclusion is stated for only some data types. The separate 'Don't save recordings' retention option is not the training opt-out; choosing it also disables voice ID.

changes.question: temporary_chat
changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-09-11 (quote not found on page; was partial): "All previously saved recordings will also be deleted. You will still be able to review the transcripts of your Alexa requests for 30 days before we begin automatically deleting them." at https://www.amazon.co.uk/b?ie=UTF8&node=27246936031 | There is no per-session incognito mode; the closest is the account-level 'Don't save recordings' option (Manage Your Alexa Data > Choose how long to save recordings), under which recordings are deleted after processing and transcripts auto-delete after 30 days, but use for improving Alexa is governed by a separate toggle so conversations may still be used for training unless that is also switched off; it can take up to 36 hours to apply.

changes.question: user_deletion
changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-09-11 (quote not found on page; was partial): "All of your voice recordings are saved by default, but you can choose to delete them at any time and there are a number of ways to do that." at https://www.amazon.co.uk/b?ie=UTF8&node=27246936031 | Individual or bulk deletion of recordings/transcripts is self-service (Review Voice History > Delete Selected Recordings, 'Alexa, delete what I just said' / 'delete everything I've ever said', auto-delete after 3 or 18 months); Amazon confirms the same Alexa Privacy dashboard covers Alexa+ interactions. Amazon account closure is handled by a help page that could not be fetched, so account deletion is not evidenced here.

changes.question: deletion_timeline
changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-09-11 (quote not found on page; was partial): "You will still be able to review the transcripts of your Alexa requests for 30 days before we begin automatically deleting them." at https://www.amazon.co.uk/b?ie=UTF8&node=27246936031 | Under the account-level Don't save recordings option, recordings are deleted after processing and transcripts are deleted automatically after 30 days, and Amazon states that manually deleted recordings and their transcripts are deleted from its cloud, but no period is stated for completing manual or account deletion. A period stated for one mode only is partial under the rubric. The quoted page is the UK Alexa privacy hub; the US page did not return text to the crawler.

changes.question: human_review_limited
changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-09-11 (quote not found on page; was partial): "Training Alexa relies in part on supervised machine learning, also referred to as “manual” or “human” review. This is an industry-standard practice conducted by trained specialists to help Alexa understand the correct interpretation of a request and provide the appropriate response in the future." at https://www.amazon.co.uk/b?ie=UTF8&node=27246937031 | Human review is disclosed for model-improvement purposes (an 'extremely small sample of requests' reviewed by trained specialists) and is on by default, with an opt-out via Manage Your Alexa Data > Help Improve Alexa or 'Alexa, turn off human review of my voice recordings'; not limited to safety/abuse cases.
